time._departure_note: Leaving port: time drops to x1 while the ship backs off the port, then steps up. Each step is [game seconds since departure, scale]; a pilot who changes the scale meanwhile keeps theirs.
time._approach_note: Coming in: time is capped as the port nears, so the last of the approach is seen at x1. Each cap is [game seconds before arrival, highest scale].

economy._note: price = base * clamp((target / stock) ^ elasticity, min, max). Stock relaxes toward target at relaxation_per_day, standing in for background traffic.

travel._note: Brachistochrone at current mass and thrust, plus fixed overheads for undock/capture. Gravity wells and orbital velocity are deliberately ignored: the co-pilot 'handles it'.

detection._note: Who can see you (sim/detection.gd, sim/systems/detection_system.gd). Each signature channel has a range in metres at which a standard sensor (factor 1) sees it: the lit drive (drive_m_per_sqrt_mw times the square root of the drive's jet power, MW: you cannot hide while burning), waste heat (heat_m_per_sqrt_kw times the root of what the ship radiates, kW: the drive's heat while burning, else its electrical loads), the transponder and running lights (fixed ranges, off when running dark), and reflected sunlight (light_m times the root of the ship's area times its albedo, falling with distance from the Sun; area_m2_per_t23 times dry mass^(2/3)). A port sees you if you are within your largest range times its sensors (port_sensors, or the place's own 'sensors'). Running dark inside a port's control_zone_m while it sees you is fined dark_fine_cr and dark_fine_rep standing with its operator, once a trip (the ports share word). The low-observable coating (coat_cr_per_t of dry mass, at stealth_yards) cuts albedo to coated_albedo; a heat sink module soaks up waste heat while running dark until full (sink_mj), and dumps it at sink_dump_kw otherwise. Checked every check_s of game time in transit.
detection._stow_note: Panels folded in while coasting (stow_panels): the hull shows stowed_area_mult of its sunlit area, and with the radiators folded only stowed_heat_mult of the waste heat gets out (the rest soaks into the structure). The solar wings make nothing. The co-pilot unfolds them for a burn: the radiators carry the drive's heat.

approach._note: The last part of every trip to a port (sim/navigation.gd add_approach), flown in the port's own frame. Over the last window_s before the ship reaches the port, it swings round from wherever the trip brings it to the corridor entry (corridor_m beyond the handover point, on the docking axis), going wide of the station (its bounding radius plus clear_margin_m) if it comes in from behind (when the cosine between its direction and the axis is under swing_cos). Then it brakes along the corridor from corridor_speed_mps to handover_speed_mps, arriving at the handover point, where the docking scene takes over. Docking ports all face view +Z (sim -Y), as in the flight scene. For a port in orbit round a body, a descent over the descent_s before that sweeps the ship down onto the port's orbit, meeting it meet_behind_m behind the port and moving with it; time drops to at most descent_time_scale for it. Trip time and propellant are unchanged.

turning._note: How the ship turns in the transit view. A hull's turn_rate_dps and turn_accel_dps2 (data/ships.json, else these defaults) hold at its stock dry mass. Angular acceleration scales with stock dry mass over what the ship weighs now (cargo, cabin and fuel included), clamped to [min_mass_factor, max_mass_factor], so a laden hauler turns slower. Turns play out in real seconds up to time compression real_time_scale; above it they speed up in proportion, so the ship keeps up with a voyage's thrust at x100,000. The drive's plume shows only once the nose is within plume_align_deg of the thrust.

damage._note: Collisions (sim/systems/damage_system.gd). Below safe_mps a bump does nothing. Above it, the energy absorbed per kilogram of ship (0.5 v^2, times the share the other body takes) over full_j_per_kg is the damage to the module hit (1 = wrecked); keel_share of that goes to the keel, and a wrecked keel is a lost ship. Damaged drives lose thrust, tanks and pods lose capacity (venting and spilling what no longer fits), radiators reject less heat, habs keep you alive for less long.

power._note: Ship electrical power (sim/power.gd, sim/systems/power_system.gd). Supply: the reactor on the drives while lit (in transit and on approach, while a site job runs, or when ordered with the 'reactor' command) and the crew section's solar wings, scaled by 1/au^2 (capped at solar_factor_max close to the Sun). Docked ships plug into shore_kw. Loads come from module data; radiator pumps draw pump_kw_per_mw for every MW of heat rejected, and the heat a lit reactor makes is its drives' heat_mw times heat_frac for the phase. A deficit drains the battery. Below shed_comms_below of charge (only while in deficit) comms and sensors shed, below shed_mining_below the rig too, and below life_warn_below life support gets a red warning first; shed_release_margin is the hysteresis. Sensors and rig draw standby_frac of their load until a job needs them. Gameplay departures (reactor fuel is free, a flat battery never hurts the crew) are recorded in docs/DESIGN.md.

cockpit._note: Cockpit alert thresholds (view/ui/cockpit_pages.gd): they colour lamps and gauges only; the rules live in the sim. Fuel and hull are fractions of nominal; heat is the ratio of heat made to heat rejected; damage is a module's 0-1 damage; power_caution_frac and power_caution_hours light the POWER caution while the battery is discharging below that charge or within that many hours of empty.
